name: Christian democracy
summary: Christian democracy is the political tradition that grew from Catholic social teaching (Rerum novarum, called its Magna Charta, and Quadragesimo anno) and from Dutch neo-Calvinism (Kuyper), with Sturzo's popularism and Maritain's personalism as its philosophers. It holds that the person and the family come before the state, that property is a natural right bound to the common good, that classes should cooperate and workers organise, that subsidiarity limits every higher body, and that democracy rests on natural rights and conscience. It is socially conservative on family and life questions.
scope: The tradition as its defining sources present it: the Catholic Encyclopedia's account of Christian democracy as the Catholic social movement launched by Rerum novarum, Kalyvas's scholarship on the party phenomenon, and the SEP's account of Maritain's influence on Christian Democratic parties. Answers rest on Rerum novarum, Quadragesimo anno, Maritain's Rights of Man and Natural Law, Kuyper's Lectures on Calvinism and Sturzo's Church and State. The EPP programme, Wikipedia and Centesimus annus (which no defining source ties to the name) are not used for any answer. Parties' platforms, later market-liberal drift and integralism are other subjects.

sources.title: Christian democracy

sources.title: Rerum novarum (Encyclical of Pope Leo XIII on Capital and Labor, 1891)
sources.author: Pope Leo XIII
sources.usedFor: Founding social encyclical, called the Magna Charta of Christian democracy: property, class cooperation, unions, wages, duties of the wealthy.

sources.title: Quadragesimo anno (Encyclical of Pope Pius XI on Reconstruction of the Social Order, 1931)
sources.author: Pope Pius XI
sources.usedFor: Subsidiarity, family wage, role of the state, economic concentration, communism.

sources.title: Jacques Maritain (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of Maritain's influence on Christian Democratic parties.

sources.title: The Rights of Man and Natural Law (Jacques Maritain, 1944; Internet Archive scan)
sources.author: Jacques Maritain
sources.usedFor: Rights of the person and of the family, universal suffrage, parties, religious freedom, limits of the state.

sources.title: Lectures on Calvinism (Abraham Kuyper, 1898; Internet Archive copy)
sources.author: Abraham Kuyper
sources.usedFor: Neo-Calvinist strand: sovereignty of God, sphere sovereignty, forms of government, capital punishment.

sources.title: Church and State (Luigi Sturzo, 1939; Internet Archive scan)
sources.author: Luigi Sturzo
sources.usedFor: Sturzo's history of church and state, independence of the Church, the state's anti-Christian measures.

abortion-legal.rationale: Sturzo lists legalised abortion, with divorce, eugenic sterilisation and compulsory laic education, among the anti-Christian measures a secular state may enact.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Maritain says freedom of conscience in religion is a natural, inviolable right against the state.

bound-labor.rationale: Maritain says every person has the right to make decisions about choosing his work and calls forced labour tyrannical.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum novarum calls it a great mistake to suppose that class is naturally hostile to class and says capital and labour need each other.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maritain describes a Christian society as one without religious compulsion or clericalism.

conscription.rationale: Maritain says that in extreme peril the state can forcibly requisition the services of each citizen and demand that each risk his life in a just war.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Maritain calls the right of the people to choose its constitution and form of government the first and most fundamental political right.

death-penalty.rationale: Kuyper holds that God commanded capital punishment for him who sheds man's blood and that the magistrate bears this right.

decide-locally.rationale: Quadragesimo anno states the principle of subsidiarity as the most weighty principle of social philosophy: what lesser and subordinate bodies can do should not be taken over by a greater and higher one.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kuyper holds that all authority of governments on earth originates from the sovereignty of God alone.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maritain lists equality of all before the law, with an independent judiciary, among the rights of the civic person.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Maritain demands equality of all before the law with an independent judiciary and lists the right to life among the fundamental rights.

family-wage.rationale: Quadragesimo anno states that a worker's wage must be sufficient to support him and his family.

harm-principle.rationale: Maritain says the state has a moral and not merely material function and that law has an educational function to develop moral virtues.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Maritain says the rights of the family and of spiritual and religious families belong to natural law in the strictest sense, alongside the rights of individual persons.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Maritain lists the right to marry according to one's choice among the fundamental rights of the person.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kuyper treats monarchy, aristocracy and democracy alike as possible and practicable forms of government.

nation-first.rationale: Maritain looks to an organized international community above the state and says states must give up absolute sovereignty to join a federation of free peoples.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Maritain says the classical notion of state sovereignty needs rigid criticism and that states must give up absolute sovereignty in an international federation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Quadragesimo anno says government must not be thought a mere guardian of law and good order.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Sturzo lists divorce among the anti-Christian measures a secular state may enact.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Sturzo lists compulsory laic education among the anti-Christian measures a secular state may enact.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rerum novarum teaches that those who have received a large share of temporal blessings hold them as stewards of providence for the benefit of others.

one-party-rule.rationale: Maritain calls the totalitarian single-party system the worst form and catastrophe of the party system and asks a new democracy to keep political parties.

person-over-state.rationale: Maritain says the state's educative function is to help the family and not to make the child a living tool and material for the state.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Maritain says that to enter a federation of free peoples, states will have to give up the privileges of absolute sovereignty.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Quadragesimo anno says that in protecting private persons chief consideration ought to be given to the weak and the poor, repeating Rerum novarum.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Maritain says a constitution juridically formulated and an independent judiciary characterise true democracy, and Kuyper says Calvinism demanded that relations of authority be regulated under the law.

property-franchise.rationale: Maritain says universal suffrage for every adult person is one of the rights a community of free men can never give up.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum novarum derives the right to private property from nature, Quadragesimo anno says the right to own and bequeath goods must stay intact and inviolate, and Maritain lists private ownership among the fundamental rights that safeguard personal liberty.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Maritain and Quadragesimo anno require private property to be used for the common good, but Rerum novarum and Quadragesimo anno also treat ownership as a natural right the state cannot abolish, so the statement's 'only to the extent' is neither affirmed nor denied.

racial-franchise.rationale: Maritain says every adult person has the right to vote, and that public employment and professions are open to all without racial or social discrimination.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Maritain demands equality of all before the law and free access to professions without racial or social discrimination.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Maritain says that with respect to the state a person is free to choose his religious path and that freedom of conscience is a natural, inviolable right.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maritain roots the rights of the person in natural law and in the communion of all in human nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kuyper holds that no one on earth can claim authority over others except as laid on him by God, and says Calvinism demanded that relations between spheres of authority be regulated under the law, creating constitutional public law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Quadragesimo anno says the state ought to be the supreme arbiter free from all partiality, intent on the common good, and condemns its capture by economic powers.

state-harmful.rationale: Quadragesimo anno says the state ought to sit on high like a queen and supreme arbiter, so it cannot be abolished.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Maritain denies the state any authority over conscience or to impose any religious faith, and Sturzo lists compulsory laic education among anti-Christian state measures.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Sturzo describes the Church as a spiritual society independent of the state, and Maritain says the state may not legislate on divine matters or impose any religious faith.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Maritain holds that diverse political parties correspond to the natural diversity of views and rejects the single-party system.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rerum novarum counts the moderate and fair imposition of public taxes among the things that make a state prosper and objects only to excessive taxation, so taxation as such is not theft.

total-state.rationale: Maritain says the state becomes iniquitous and tyrannical if it bases civil life on forced labour or violates the rights of the family to become master of men's souls.

traditional-family.rationale: Rerum novarum calls the family a true society governed by the authority of the father and older than the state, and Maritain says a person is part of family society before political society.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum novarum calls workingmen's unions the most important of all workers' associations and says history shows the excellent results of the old guilds.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Maritain says law binds in conscience only because it is law if just and promulgated by legitimate authority.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Quadragesimo anno attacks the concentration of immense power and despotic economic dictatorship in a few hands as an economic dictatorship.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rerum novarum says the law's policy should be to induce as many people as possible to become owners.

women-suffrage.rationale: Maritain says every adult human person has the right to vote and that civic rights belong to all.

missingStatements.text: Public decisions should be taken at the lowest level that can handle them, with higher bodies stepping in only when lower ones cannot.
missingStatements.rationale: Subsidiarity is stated in Quadragesimo anno as the most weighty principle of social philosophy.

missingStatements.text: The death penalty should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Christian democracy is documented as opposing capital punishment as part of a consistent life ethic.
missingStatements.declined: Documented only as a secondary position and not a defining one; kept out to keep the bank lean.

notes: Rebuilt on the ideology's own texts after the queued review found 93 answers resting on the EPP programme alone (a party federation's platform, so a coatrack) and 29 on Wikipedia alone: each was nulled with its history kept. Themes searched in the local texts: property, wages and unions, strikes, taxation, class relations, state role and subsidiarity, family, church and state, religious freedom, suffrage and parties, rule of law, forced labour, war and conscription, capital punishment. Most statements on markets, welfare, immigration, foreign policy, technology, gender and ecology have no position in these texts and stay null; Centesimus annus (1991) covers many of them but no defining source names it, so it is left out. The EPP programme's support for pooling sovereignty was dropped from missingStatements for the same reason.

keyFigures.role: Philosopher of integral humanism and personalism whose ideas shaped post-war Christian democracy.
keyFigures.quote: Maritain had a significant influence in the development of and advocacy for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and his political philosophy had a substantial impact on ‘Christian Democratic’ parties
